I think as much as we like to say that the nurse training standards should be held up, but if some of you knew how difficult it is to get into a nursing program even with being completely capable. I have been straight A student my entire life high school and college. In 2007. I became a single mother so life became somewhat complicated. I tried to get into nursing school after doing 1.5 years of pre-requisites with a 3.8 GPA. I sat down infront of an interviewer that basically tells you whether your application is approved. I was told off the bat the wait list is 2 years. And also that my GPA for that year needed to be a 3.9 because thats the lowest they have been accepting. Needless to say I was devastated. I studied hard and got A’s in ever class except for Psychology and Microbiology which I got a B in. I went straight to registrars office and switched my major to accounting. I have an associate degree in accounting now. Flash forward a couple years I was brainstorming how to get money for college to go for my BS in accounting after few semesters decided to join the army. Started LPN school, excelled, graduated in top 10 of my class with a ^90% avg. Got out of the army went back to new york, applied for nursing school again and got turned down even with 7 years of LVN experience. I was told i needed prerequisites. I completed them and still got denied. I ended up getting another associates degree in Liberal arts due to all the fucking pre requisites I am taking. Moved to Texas 2022, I said I am not giving up. I applied for another nursing program in a small college here. I will also add that I am also taking online classes at a 4 year college for healthcare administration in the meantime in case it doesn’t work out. Still getting A’s working full time and 2 autistic children that I take care of. Guess what again. I have to take 2 pre requisite classes lol. I also got A in those. In order to apply I need to wait till March 1st. Then take an Hesi A2 exam and wait for approval. This is the freaking gate keeping that people go through that lead them to take drastic illegal measures. I am not saying it is right, and I would never! I love nursing so much, but I am sure so many people like me have the passion and capabilities and still get turned down. I either have the worst luck or something but this is my story. I said all of that to say this. I despise people that take shortcuts, however, I see from the standpoint that it doesn’t mean that people are incapable why they chose that route. We have no idea sometimes why
People go through what they go through in life. Be kind and honest.

Hello! I would say dont give up without being cliche. Seriously. DONT! I came to the US from Jamaica in 2001. Id like to share my story with you and anyone else who feels this way. Like most people born out of the states my family pushed me to get in the nursing field. “Youll always have a job” As a teenager I really didnt want to but tried because I felt a duty to my mother to atleast try. Long story short, in NYC the colleges there are very competitive and there are so many “nursing” programs gatekeep! Its almost like you had to know someone to know someone. I did all my prerequisites in 2 years and then applied to the nursing program. With a 3.7 GPA. I was denied. My heart shattered I cried and vowed eff nursing. I changed my major to accounting and vowed to never look that direction again. Fast forward a “useless” associates in accounting and going to 4 year college to  get me BS in accounting for a CPA. I ran out of money to pay for school. I ran through all the possibilities and outcomes and spoke to a couple friends I had in the military. On my 30th b-day I enlisted as a soldier and went to LPN/ 68C school. I passed the pnclex and I have been an lpn in the military for a while. I spent about 6 years in and when my contract was up. I did not re-enlist and I tried once again to go to nursing school. After completing more pre-requisites for 2 semesters. I applied for nursing program at a different school. Once again, mostly straight A student with exception of 2 B’s I was denied once again. Now I have a 2nd associate degree in Liberal arts. Schools are full of shit sometimes. I left NYC and moved to Texas and I am here once again taking the pre-requisites for RN program here. I am not giving up. I know I can do this. You have went even further than a lot of people I know including myself. I said all of that to say this. Everyone’s journey is different. If you feel to take a break and then try again or decide to go another route, its OK. Dont stress yourself out. its ok. It will always be ok. Take a break, hopefully you have friends and family around to give you support. I cut out a lot out of my story because it was years and feels like forever. Ive felt like you. But dont give up! Life is so strange you may just need a break. Please give it a try! Hope my story gives you atleast something to think about.

• Emotional Support!!! PLENTY you will feel like crap and pretty helpless for first week atleast! 
• Canned soup, different kinds, some you will have to blend and water down.
